label: input token x during the original phase
explanation: Token detector: fires whenever the input is the letter x at an original-phase step (any position, any L). It does not fire on x when x is fed back as input during the copy phase (only 140 negligible copy-phase activations), on the delimiter, or on any other token. Magnitude is strongest (max) when x is the first token, weakens at later positions (about 0.55-0.9 of max), and is lower again for repeated occurrences of x in the same sequence (in_first==0 cases sit in the lower quartiles).

issues: The core predicate holds. On test: precision 0.99998, recall 0.9987, F1 0.9994, mass recall 0.99997. All 107,536 dev activations have in_tok == x. The delimiter has 0 activations and the copy phase has 140, all near zero (about 0.00-0.03 of max) and carrying 0.0% of the mass.

The 136 test misses are all the same tiny copy-phase pattern: x is fed back as the first copied token (recall_idx 1, right after <DEL>) in sequences that start with x. These are activations of about 0.01 of max. They are systematic but carry no mass.
There are only 2 test false positives, both at the last original position (t=8). That is scattered noise.

One magnitude claim is too generous. Dividing activation mass by active steps at each position gives a per-step mean, relative to t=0, of about 0.83 at t=3, 0.72 at t=4, 0.59 at t=5, 0.43 at t=6, 0.30 at t=7 and 0.21 at t=8. So magnitude keeps falling steadily with position, well below the stated 'about 0.55-0.9 of max'.
The other claims check out. Magnitude peaks at the first token (t=0). Repeated x tokens (in_first==0) are weaker: 6.9% of the mass on 9.4% of the active steps.
